text: The review band from Lesson 7 needs a human because getting it wrong in either direction carries a real cost — this lesson is what a steward actually does about that.

A false positive merges two different people — one customer's data gets contaminated with a stranger's history. A false negative leaves a true duplicate unmerged — quieter, but it defeats the whole point of MDM for that record. A human steward, with context an algorithm doesn't have, is the right tool for the uncertain middle band.

Confirm or reject the candidate pair based on the evidence. Fix the source data when the real problem turns out to be a typo, not the match logic. Tune the rules — a pattern in how reviews land is feedback that improves the automated matching over time.

A pair lands in the queue because its score fell between the two thresholds. The steward decides: merge, reject, or needs more data. That decision resolves the case and becomes a labeled example for future rule tuning.
That closes Chapter 2 — matching and consolidation. Chapter 3 moves from mechanics to domains: customer master, product master, vendor master, and more, starting next.
